name: THE JOHNS HOPKINS UNIVERSITY APPLIED PHYSICS LABORATORY LLC
naics_description: RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT IN THE PHYSICAL, ENGINEERING, AND LIFE SCIENCES (EXCEPT NANOTECHNOLOGY AND BIOTECHNOLOGY)
brief_text:
Four detectors flagged this entity. Benford's law analysis of leading digits in award amounts showed a p-value of 0.30, indicating the distribution is consistent with expected patterns and not anomalous. Modification growth on contract N0002413D6400 revealed extreme acceleration: the award's modifications grew at a ratio of 13,104 times, vastly exceeding the NAICS peer average of 57 times, with a z-score of 23.67. Isolation Forest identified the entity as a multivariate outlier with a score of 0.93, driven by its massive lifetime dollar total, high award count, concentration among two agencies, and very high modification frequency. Sole-source concentration showed 1,439 of 1,493 awards were sole-source, representing 96.4 percent, compared to a NAICS median of 7.7 percent.

The entity has obligated 7.8 billion dollars across 1,494 lifetime awards. The worst-performing contract modification ratio of 13,104 compares to a peer z-score of 23.67 standard deviations above the mean. The isolation anomaly score of 0.93 reflects a feature vector including log total dollars of 9.89, modification frequency of 0.78, and competition ratio of 0.036. Sole-source awards comprise 96.4 percent of the portfolio versus a peer median of 7.7 percent, yielding a z-score of 3.72.

Johns Hopkins APL is a federally funded research and development center with a decades-long relationship to the Department of Defense, which explains the concentration in two agencies and high sole-source award prevalence in this specialized sector. The extreme modification growth and multivariate outlier status warrant scrutiny, but the entity's scale, mission criticality, and FFRDC status are material context. Benford's test showed no digit anomaly. The small peer group in this NAICS may inflate z-scores for legitimate structural differences.
